task.title: Materialize the next due schedule through deterministic CLI JSON
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/849 by exposing atomic next-due schedule/task materialization without widening CLI authority.
acceptance_criteria: Validate one caller-owned task identity before storage access and delegate the explicit cutoff to ScheduleStore::materialize_next_due.
Emit the complete materialized schedule projection or explicit null when no work is eligible.
Fail closed with schedule_materialization_failed and no partial stdout, orphan task, generated identity, clock, dispatch, permission, or execution authority.

attempts.diagnostic: CLI integration tests failed because materialize-next was not a recognized schedule subcommand.
attempts.patch: Added focused command tests for deterministic selection, empty work, invalid task identity, task collision, persistence, and storage failure.

attempts.summary: Exposed the bounded atomic operation and refactored its response shape.
attempts.diagnostic: The atomic kernel operation existed, but automation had no deterministic JSON boundary and would otherwise need custom persistence integration.
attempts.patch: Added schedule materialize-next, reused the next-schedule response type and complete inspection projection, and documented exact success and failure behavior.

attempts.summary: Preserved exact-head review discipline after a false-green status.
attempts.diagnostic: The initial CodeRabbit run reached its review limit even though the status appeared green; later substantive review suggested only a low-value serialization helper extraction.
attempts.patch: Kept auto-merge disabled through the stated cooldown, deliberately resumed review once capacity returned, and retained the simple shared response shape without an unnecessary behavioral change.

outcome.summary: Automation can materialize the earliest due intent and create its caller-identified inert task atomically through compact deterministic JSON.

lessons: Expose the kernel's atomic operation directly rather than reconstructing selection and two-stream persistence in scripts.
Validate caller-owned identity before opening writable storage and emit no partial JSON on failure.
A green rate-limited status is not review evidence; wait for capacity and require a genuine substantive review of the exact head.
